raw_cv.summary: Streaming systems engineer with 5 years working on video pipelines: encoding ladders, packaging, CDN behaviour and low-latency delivery. I care about the bit that arrives when it should, not just the bit that arrives. I have worked on live events where a ten-second delay was the whole problem, and I have shipped VOD catalogues that had to be transcoded once, not six times.

work_description: Live encoding pipeline design and 24/7 monitoring of delivery health.
Latency work: packaging, CDN routing and player buffering behaviour.
Automation for restarts and failover of the ingest layer.
Transcoding of the VOD catalogue and per-title optimisation.
Subtitles, DRM and playback compatibility across devices.

description: Rebuilt the live packaging path and cut perceived glass-to-glass latency.
Automated the per-title transcode policy so new content is encoded correctly without a human checking.
Added synthetic monitoring that plays the stream like a viewer would.

items: I care about the experience on a phone on a bad network, not about the spec sheet.
I measure end to end, from the encoder to the screen.
I document the failover steps so a tired operator can follow them.
I keep a short list of what breaks first when things go wrong.

My background is in video delivery rather than in the platform side of streaming. I have worked with packaging and encoding in depth, but I am still building my understanding of the business models and analytics side of the business.
Un codec nou fara un plan de rollback, este o interventie, nu o optimizare.
Testarea sintetica prinde degradarea inainte de reclamanii, cu conditii reale de retea.
Latenta se pierde in etape mici, si se cauta la fiecare etapa, nu la final.

raw_cv.summary: Security architect with 14 years designing defences for banks, insurers and SaaS platforms. I am the person who turns 'we should be more secure' into a concrete threat model, a control set and a plan engineers can implement. At a European bank I lead the security architecture for the cloud programme covering 400 workloads, and I have closed hundreds of high-severity findings before production. I believe security earns its budget by being a good engineering partner, not a gatekeeper.

work_description: Own security architecture for a 400-workload cloud programme across AWS and Azure.
Introduced threat modelling as a standard step; high-severity findings in production fell by more than half.
Designed the IAM and secrets-management model; removed standing privileged access for 900 engineers.
Led the response architecture for incident playbooks and tabletop exercises with the CISO.
Application and network security architecture; ran the secure SDLC rollout.
Application and infrastructure testing for banks and public sector; the hands-on years that taught me what breaks.

items: Zero trust (2021-2023): replaced VPN with identity-aware access for 900 engineers; access incidents down 55%.
SIEM consolidation (2022): 1,400 rules rationalised to 300 high-signal detections; analyst fatigue measurably reduced.
Secure SDLC (2017): embedded automated scanning and threat models into delivery; escaped defects down sharply.
Developer enablement (2023): a six-module internal course completed by 500 engineers; Git secret leaks down 80%.
Regulatory readiness (2024): led the security workstream for DORA readiness with no critical gaps.
Engineer first: security work lands only when it is usable; I design controls teams can adopt without a fight.
Threat-informed: I start from realistic adversaries and attack paths, then prioritise controls by risk reduced per unit of effort.
Measurable: findings closed before production, MTTR for security incidents, and coverage of critical assets are tracked, not guessed.
Cloud security (2019-2024): architecture and guardrails for 400 workloads across AWS and Azure, including network segmentation and centralized logging.
Identity programme (2021-2023): zero-trust access for 900 engineers; removed standing privileged access and reduced access incidents by 55%.
Detection engineering (2022): consolidated the SIEM and rationalised 1,400 rules to 300 high-signal detections.
Developer enablement (2023): six-module course completed by 500 engineers; Git secret leaks down 80%.
Third-party risk (2024): a vendor security review workflow that shortened onboarding while raising the bar.
Platforms: AWS/Azure security services, Kubernetes hardening, Terraform security modules, WAF, KMS
Detection: Splunk, Sentinel, EDR, vulnerability scanners, SAST/DAST/SCA in CI
Frameworks: MITRE ATT&CK;, NIST CSF, ISO 27001, OWASP ASVS/SAMM, DORA
Design, not decree: I sit in the design reviews and offer patterns, so security is built in rather than bolted on.
Risk in business terms: I translate findings into likelihood, impact and cost so owners can prioritise sensibly.
Automate the boring: scanners and policy-as-code in CI catch the easy issues so people can focus on the hard ones.
Blameless learning: incidents are studied, not punished, so people report early.
CISSP (2016), CCSP (2019), AWS Security Specialty (2022).
OWASP chapter volunteer; DefCamp mentor; occasional speaker on cloud security.
Coached 4 engineers into security-architect roles.

Zero-trust identity (2021-2023): VPN gave everyone broad network access. We replaced it with identity-aware proxies and short-lived credentials, mapping and closing 60 legacy exceptions. Access-related incidents fell by more than half and engineers got faster access.

Detection rationalisation (2022): three SIEM tools and 1,400 noisy rules. We consolidated the tooling and reduced rules to 300 high-signal detections tied to real attack techniques, measurably cutting analyst fatigue.

Developer security (2023): a six-module internal course and automated secret scanning in CI; Git secret leaks dropped roughly 80%.
Threat-informed defence: spend the effort where a realistic adversary would actually go.
Usable controls: a control teams route around is worse than no control, because it looks like protection.
Least privilege by default: standing access is a liability; make the safe path the easy path.
Assume breach: design for detection and containment, not only for prevention.

: CISO and Head of Security Engineering - on request

Sergiu Istrate
Frontend Platform Lead - design systems & monorepo - 11 years
Bucharest | +40 726 447 663 | sergiu.istrate.fe@gmail.com | github.com/sergiu-istrate
PROFILE
Frontend platform lead with 11 years building the layer teams build on: design systems, component libraries,
build tooling and the conventions that keep twenty engineers producing consistent work. I have been the
person who removes friction rather than adding process, which is why the teams I worked with shipped faster,
not slower. I still write production code most days, because a platform lead who stops coding drifts.
EXPERIENCE
Frontend Platform Lead 2020 - Present
Product group - Bucharest
(cid:127) Own the design system used by six product teams and about 200 screens.
(cid:127) Migrated the monorepo to a faster build with remote caching.
(cid:127) Introduced visual regression testing and accessibility gates in CI.
(cid:127) Ran the hiring loop for frontend engineers and mentored four of them.
Senior Frontend Engineer 2016 - 2020
Product company - Bucharest
(cid:127) Built complex web applications in React and TypeScript.
(cid:127) Owned the frontend architecture decisions for a major product line.
Frontend Developer 2013 - 2016
Digital agency - Bucharest
(cid:127) Delivered client web applications, mostly React and some Angular.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, some Rust for tooling
Frameworks: React, Vue, Next.js, Vite, Storybook
Platform: monorepos (Turborepo/Nx), CI/CD, bundle analysis, testing
Quality: accessibility (WCAG), visual regression, performance budgets
SELECTED OUTCOMES
(cid:127) Cut the median build time from 9 minutes to under 2, which changed how often people could afford to run
the test suite.
(cid:127) Adoption of the design system across six teams within three quarters, measured by component usage in
code review.
(cid:127) Introduced accessibility gates that stopped a measurable number of regressions.


(cid:127) Created the frontend guild that now runs reviews and shares patterns across teams.
HOW I WORK
(cid:127) I write a short proposal before a big platform change, with the cost stated honestly.
(cid:127) I would rather ship a small useful tool than a large unfinished platform.
(cid:127) I measure adoption instead of declaring a platform successful.
(cid:127) I keep the escape hatch open so teams are never forced into the wrong abstraction.
A NOTE ON WEAKNESSES
I have spent years in JavaScript and TypeScript, and I am not a deep systems programmer, even though I
have started writing Rust for build tooling. I also know that my instinct for platform work can slow teams down
if it is not kept in check by real usage data.
EDUCATION
B.Sc. Computer Science, University of Bucharest. Romanian native, English C1, French B1.
HOW I BUILT THINGS
(cid:127) Adoption over announcement: I measured whether teams used the system instead of assuming they
did.
(cid:127) Escape hatches: every platform primitive could be bypassed, so nobody is forced into a wrong
abstraction.
(cid:127) Cost stated early: every proposal said what it would take to maintain, not only to build.
(cid:127) Small and shipped: a useful tool in a month beats a platform in a year.
DESIGN SYSTEM WORK
(cid:127) Tokens first: colour, spacing and type scale agreed before a single component existed.
(cid:127) Accessibility baked in: contrast and focus states checked in the design review, not at the end.
(cid:127) Documentation with examples: real usage samples beat a page of prop tables.
(cid:127) Deprecation policy: components were versioned and old ones were removed on a schedule.
PLATFORM AND TOOLING
(cid:127) Moved three teams into one monorepo with independent release permissions.
(cid:127) Introduced remote caching and parallel test execution in CI.
(cid:127) Set bundle size and performance budgets that the build actually enforces.
(cid:127) Introduced visual regression testing with a curated set of meaningful screens.


LEADERSHIP
(cid:127) I run the frontend guild: one meeting a month, shared patterns, no hierarchy.
(cid:127) I reviewed the frontend loop and wrote a practical hiring rubric.
(cid:127) I mentored four engineers, two of whom now lead their own teams.
(cid:127) I gave recurring talks inside the company about platform thinking.
INTERESTS AND CURRENT LEARNING
(cid:127) I maintain a small open-source library for typed design tokens, which taught me a lot about API design.
(cid:127) I am learning Rust properly, mostly because I wanted to replace a brittle Node script with something faster.
(cid:127) I restore and resynthesise old synthesizers, which is a completely different kind of debugging.
(cid:127) I read a lot of interface history, which explains most of my opinions.
A NOTE ON WEAKNESSES
My instincts are biased towards platform work, and I have had to learn that not every problem deserves a
platform. I am also a slower writer of documentation than I would like, which is why I now force myself to write
the proposal before the code, rather than after. And my JavaScript depth is in the framework era rather than in
the platform era, which I have had to correct for through reading and small contributions.
WHAT I LOOK FOR IN THE NEXT ROLE
(cid:127) A team where the platform is treated as a product with real users, not as a cost centre.
(cid:127) Enough influence to push back on priorities, and enough humility to be wrong about them.
(cid:127) A product with real users, so the value of the work is visible and not abstract.
RESPONSABILITATI ACTUALE
(cid:127) Ownership asupra sistemului de design folosit de sase echipe de produs.
(cid:127) Definirea strategiei tehnice front-end si a regulilor de calitate pentru monorepo.
(cid:127) Mentenanta lantului de livrare si a bugetelor de performanta.
(cid:127) Coordonarea procesului de angajare si de integrare a noilor ingineri front-end.
CE AM INVOCAT DINALTE ORGANIZATII
(cid:127) In 2016 am mostenit un sistem de design care nu avea documentatie si era folosit inconsistent; l-am
reconstruit de la zero in opt luni.
(cid:127) Am mutat trei echipe separate intr-un monorepo si am platit pretul de tranzitie prin opt luni de lucru
aproape exclusiv de infrastructura.
(cid:127) Am invatat ca migrarile de platforma au nevoie de un plan de iesire, altfel devin un proiect permanent.


MASURAREA IMPACTULUI
(cid:127) Timp de construire redus de la 9 minute la sub 2, masurat pe CI, cu efect direct asupra frecventei cu care
echipele ruleaza testele.
(cid:127) Adoptia componentelor, urmarita prin revizii de cod, si nu prin numarul de componente publicate.
(cid:127) Reducerea regresiilor de accesibilitate dupa introducerea verificarii automate, masurata in bilete, nu in
impresii.
CE IMI PLACE SA FAC
(cid:127) Sa reduc timpul de anteptare al unui dezvoltator, pentru ca acesta este un cost real, care nu apare in
niciun raport.
(cid:127) Sa pun in scris propunerile mele, pentru ca deciziile sa fie discutabile, nu doar impun.
(cid:127) Sa mentin standarde care sunt stricte dar clare, pentru ca oamenii sa stie exact ce se asteapta de la ei.
UN GAND DE FINAL
Ingineria front-end s-a schimbat mult in unsprezece ani, dar principiul a ramas: interfana este produsul, iar
produsul se ridica in standardul in care il construiesti. Am ales sa lucrez pe unelte si platforme pentru ca imi
place sa vad cum o decizie de arhitectura se transforma in timp economisit pentru zeci de oameni, iar asta
este un efect pe care il pot explica in cuvinte simple.

(cid:127) Adoption over announcement: I measured whether teams used the system instead of assuming they
did.
(cid:127) Escape hatches: every platform primitive could be bypassed, so nobody is forced into a wrong
abstraction.
(cid:127) Cost stated early: every proposal said what it would take to maintain, not only to build.
(cid:127) Small and shipped: a useful tool in a month beats a platform in a year.
DESIGN SYSTEM WORK
(cid:127) Tokens first: colour, spacing and type scale agreed before a single component existed.
(cid:127) Accessibility baked in: contrast and focus states checked in the design review, not at the end.
(cid:127) Documentation with examples: real usage samples beat a page of prop tables.
(cid:127) Deprecation policy: components were versioned and old ones were removed on a schedule.
PLATFORM AND TOOLING
(cid:127) Moved three teams into one monorepo with independent release permissions.
(cid:127) Introduced remote caching and parallel test execution in CI.
(cid:127) Set bundle size and performance budgets that the build actually enforces.
(cid:127) Introduced visual regression testing with a curated set of meaningful screens.


LEADERSHIP
(cid:127) I run the frontend guild: one meeting a month, shared patterns, no hierarchy.
(cid:127) I reviewed the frontend loop and wrote a practical hiring rubric.
(cid:127) I mentored four engineers, two of whom now lead their own teams.
(cid:127) I gave recurring talks inside the company about platform thinking.
INTERESTS AND CURRENT LEARNING
(cid:127) I maintain a small open-source library for typed design tokens, which taught me a lot about API design.
(cid:127) I am learning Rust properly, mostly because I wanted to replace a brittle Node script with something faster.
(cid:127) I restore and resynthesise old synthesizers, which is a completely different kind of debugging.
(cid:127) I read a lot of interface history, which explains most of my opinions.
A NOTE ON WEAKNESSES
My instincts are biased towards platform work, and I have had to learn that not every problem deserves a
platform. I am also a slower writer of documentation than I would like, which is why I now force myself to write
the proposal before the code, rather than after. And my JavaScript depth is in the framework era rather than in
the platform era, which I have had to correct for through reading and small contributions.
WHAT I LOOK FOR IN THE NEXT ROLE
(cid:127) A team where the platform is treated as a product with real users, not as a cost centre.
(cid:127) Enough influence to push back on priorities, and enough humility to be wrong about them.
(cid:127) A product with real users, so the value of the work is visible and not abstract.
RESPONSABILITATI ACTUALE
(cid:127) Ownership asupra sistemului de design folosit de sase echipe de produs.
(cid:127) Definirea strategiei tehnice front-end si a regulilor de calitate pentru monorepo.
(cid:127) Mentenanta lantului de livrare si a bugetelor de performanta.
(cid:127) Coordonarea procesului de angajare si de integrare a noilor ingineri front-end.
CE AM INVOCAT DINALTE ORGANIZATII
(cid:127) In 2016 am mostenit un sistem de design care nu avea documentatie si era folosit inconsistent; l-am
reconstruit de la zero in opt luni.
(cid:127) Am mutat trei echipe separate intr-un monorepo si am platit pretul de tranzitie prin opt luni de lucru
aproape exclusiv de infrastructura.
(cid:127) Am invatat ca migrarile de platforma au nevoie de un plan de iesire, altfel devin un proiect permanent.


MASURAREA IMPACTULUI
(cid:127) Timp de construire redus de la 9 minute la sub 2, masurat pe CI, cu efect direct asupra frecventei cu care
echipele ruleaza testele.
(cid:127) Adoptia componentelor, urmarita prin revizii de cod, si nu prin numarul de componente publicate.
(cid:127) Reducerea regresiilor de accesibilitate dupa introducerea verificarii automate, masurata in bilete, nu in
impresii.
CE IMI PLACE SA FAC
(cid:127) Sa reduc timpul de anteptare al unui dezvoltator, pentru ca acesta este un cost real, care nu apare in
niciun raport.
(cid:127) Sa pun in scris propunerile mele, pentru ca deciziile sa fie discutabile, nu doar impun.
(cid:127) Sa mentin standarde care sunt stricte dar clare, pentru ca oamenii sa stie exact ce se asteapta de la ei.
UN GAND DE FINAL
Ingineria front-end s-a schimbat mult in unsprezece ani, dar principiul a ramas: interfana este produsul, iar
produsul se ridica in standardul in care il construiesti. Am ales sa lucrez pe unelte si platforme pentru ca imi
place sa vad cum o decizie de arhitectura se transforma in timp economisit pentru zeci de oameni, iar asta
este un efect pe care il pot explica in cuvinte simple.

raw_cv.summary: Senior Backend Engineer with 7 years of experience designing and operating Java-based microservices on AWS for fintech, betting and enterprise SaaS products. Currently at Flutter Entertainment (Betfair Romania), owning 4 payment & risk services processing 2M+ transactions/day with 99.95% availability. Strong in Java 17 / Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes and Terraform. Known for cutting p95 latency, cleaning up legacy monoliths, and mentoring juniors. AWS Solutions Architect Associate certified.

work_description: Own 4 Spring Boot 3 microservices in payments & risk domain (Java 17, PostgreSQL, Kafka), handling 2M+ settled bets / payments daily; on-call rotation, SLO 99.95%.
Led migration of legacy monolith settlement module to AWS Lambda + SQS + RDS; cut infrastructure cost by 31% and deployment time from 45 min to 9 min.
Reduced p95 API latency from 820 ms to 510 ms (-38%) via query tuning, Redis caching and Kafka consumer rebalancing; added Grafana + PagerDuty alerts.
Introduced contract testing (Pact) and testcontainers-based integration tests; flaky-test rate dropped from 14% to 3%, release cadence moved to weekly.
Mentor 3 mid/junior engineers; run design reviews and interview loop for backend hiring (12 hires in 2 years).
Built KYC onboarding & document-verification APIs for a UK fintech client (Java 11, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, S3); served 300k+ onboardings in first year.
Designed event-driven flow with Kafka + SQS for ID-check callbacks; eliminated polling jobs and reduced onboarding drop-off by 12%.
Set up GitLab CI + SonarQube + Terraform pipelines across 3 environments; achieved 80%+ unit coverage and zero-downtime ECS deployments.
Worked Agile/Scrum in a distributed team (Cluj + London); demoed to stakeholders, wrote ADRs and OpenAPI specs.
Maintained property-management SaaS modules (Java 8, Hibernate, Oracle SQL) used by 2,000+ US property managers.
Fixed 150+ bugs and implemented 20+ small features (billing, reporting); improved batch-job runtime by 25% via indexing and pagination.
Wrote JSP / REST endpoints and JasperReports templates; participated in code reviews and quarterly releases.

raw_cv.summary: In-house counsel with 17 years spanning top-tier private practice and industry. Currently Head of Legal at eMAG, Bucharest: lead 9 lawyers covering commercial, tech sourcing, GDPR, competition and litigation for group operations in 4 countries. Negotiated framework deals to EUR 100M, ran 3 dawn-raid preparations, and own the group privacy programme (40 processing registers, DPIAs, DPA with 200 vendors). Earlier: Senior Associate at NND KP (M&A/tech) and counsel at Vodafone Romania. Admitted to Bucharest Bar (2008), INPPA mentor. Style: business-first dra fting, short memos with clear risk/recommendation, calm in board fights.

work_description: Lead team of 9 (4 senior, 3 mid, 2 junior) + panel of 6 law firms; budget EUR 1.8M; SLAs with 5 internal clients.
Own all commercial contract ing: marketplace T&Cs for 50k sellers, logistics SLAs, cloud/MSA stack (AWS, GCP); playbooks cut negotiation cycles 30%.
Privacy programme: records of processing for 40 flows, 120 DPIAs, cookie overhaul, 2 ANSPDCP inspections closed with warnings only.
Litigation portfolio: 400 active files (consumer, IP, competition); win rate 82%; key precedent on platform liability (2022, final).
M&A support: 2 acq uisitions (due d iligence + SPA/W&I;); Day-1 integration checklists with finance/IT.
Tech procurement (network + IT, EUR 40M/year): RAN swaps, managed services, handset supply; risk allocation under pressure.
Regulatory: ANCOM consultations (net neutrality, spectrum), 5 ANCOM sanctions appealed (3 won/2 reduced).
Consumer claims automation with care team; complaint-to-court ratio -35%.
M&A closings in telecom/retail (EUR 5-60M): DD, SPAs, shareholders pacts, merger filings.
Drafted MVNO and outsourcing templates reused firm-wide; secondment to client legal team (4 months).
Civil/commercial litigation first instance; enforcement files; learned bundles and deadlines the hard way.

items: Marketplace T&C overhaul + 50k seller migration: Owner, with product. Outcome: Zero injunctions; disputes -25%.
Cloud consolidation (2 hyperscalers): Lead negotiator. Outcome: EUR 30M TCV; liability caps held.
ANSPDCP inspection 2022 (cookies + profiling): Owner + DPO. Outcome: Warning + plan; no fine.
Platform-liability litigation (2021-22): Strategy + counsel team. Outcome: Final win; precedent cited twice.
Acquisition of 2 last-mile firms: Legal lead. Outcome: Closed in 5 months incl. merger filing.
Dawn-raid readiness (competition): Owner. Outcome: 3 mock raids; 60 staff trained.
RAN swap programme (prior role): Contracts lead. Outcome: EUR 40M; LDs collected once.
Consumer ADR framework: Co-owner with care. Outcome: Court filings -35%.
Liability cap (SaaS/cloud): 12 months fees, carve-outs for IP/wilful. Fallback: 24 months with super-cap for data loss.
SLA credits: 10-30% service credits, termination at 3 fails. Fallback: Extended credits + root-cause audits.
DPA / sub-processors: Prior notice + objection, 30-day exit. Fallback: General authorisation with annual list.
IP in custom dev: Assignment to group, moral rights waiver. Fallback: Licence-back to vendor for tooling.
Price adjustment: Fixed 12 months, CPI cap 5%. Fallback: Benchmark + renegotiation trigger.
Termination for convenience: 90 days, paid wind-down. Fallback: 180 days on strategic deals.
Internal academy: 12 sessions/year (contract clinics, GDPR for product managers, dawn-raid drills, e-commerce compliance).
Regulatory log: 5 ANCOM consultations answered (2015-18), 3 ANSPDCP notifications handled, 2 merger filings (cleared Phase I), 1 competition follow-up closed without charges.
Template library owned: 40 models (MSA, DPA, marketplace rules, logistics SLA, influencer terms) with version control and owner matrix - onboarding time for new lawyers 3 months to 5 weeks.

custom_sections.section_title: Five Negotiations I Remember (What Actually Moved Them)
items: Hyperscaler renewal: vendor opened at +22%. We benchmarked with 2 peers, unbundled support tiers, and traded a case-study logo for holding the price flat - signed at +2% with better SLAs.
Logistics SLA: carrier refused penalties. We proposed shared upside instead - 50/50 of proven savings from OTIF gains - and got penalties accepted as the mirror term.
DPA standoff: US vendor would not move on sub-processors. We mapped the 3 risky flows to an EU-hosted alternative and walked them through switching costs - objection rights granted in 48h.
Founder acquisition: seller wanted full cash at close. Earn-out tied to 2 KPIs they controlled (retention + uptime) bridged a 20% valuation gap; paid in full year one.
Works-council consultation on monitoring tools: involved employee reps before procurement, published the DPIA summary - consultation closed in 3 weeks instead of 3 months.
Pro bono: 2 matters/year taken personally - 2023: eviction defence for an elderly tenant (won, payment plan ordered); 2024: GDPR complaint for a journalists NGO (upheld, controller warned).
Bar activity: INPPA mentor for 4 juniors (all admitted, 2 with top marks); Bucharest Bar professional-training lecturer on tech contracts (6 sessions, 180 attendees).
Teaching: guest lectures at ASE Business Law master (platform regulation, yearly since 2021) and University of Bucharest LL.M. (data protection clinic, 2022-2024).
Pipeline: article on AI Act interplay with GDPR for recommender systems (draft with a former student, submission autumn 2025).

MSA + order forms (3 variants by spend), DPA with transfer module selector, marketplace seller T&Cs + strike policy, logistics SLA with OTIF Ladder, cloud order form (credits + committed use), influencer/affiliate terms, sponsorship pack, NDA one-way/mutual (RO/EN), intercompany service agreement, employee invention assignment, whistleblowing policy + reporting flow. Each with owner, review date and negotiation history.

I grow volume through distributor management, perfect-store execution and disciplined KPI routines. I have turned around underperforming regions by fixing coverage, coaching teams and negotiating honestly with partners. I spend my time in the field, not at head office.

work_description: Lead a region of EUR 22M turnover with 6 area managers and 120 indirect sales staff.
Grew regional volume 28% in 3 years on a flat market, with a profitable mix.
Improved weighted distribution by 12 points through coverage and must-stock discipline.
Turned around a declining sub-region by rebuilding coverage and coaching the field team; it returned to growth within 4 quarters.
Own the P&L of the region, including trade investment and distributor margins, and manage trade investment to deliver growth without eroding regional profitability.
Promoted 3 area managers and reduced field turnover by improving coaching and rewards.
Spend time in the field with each area manager, coaching on coverage, visibility and negotiation.
Conduct monthly business reviews with top distributor partners on targets, margins and execution.
Review sell-in and sell-out data, fix distribution gaps and act on the outliers.
Conduct one-to-ones, KPI reviews and development conversations, and recruit and onboard replacements quickly.
Managed an area of EUR 7M.
Built the field discipline and KPI routine that the candidate still uses.
Managed traditional trade and key accounts.
Developed the craft of selling and listening.

raw_cv.summary: Lead data scientist with 10 years turning messy business questions into decisions backed by evidence. I specialise in demand forecasting, pricing and causal inference, and I have shipped models that run in production and are trusted by operations teams. At eMAG I lead a team of five covering supply chain and marketing science; my forecasting work directly informs purchasing decisions worth hundreds of millions of lei a year. I care as much about how a result changes behaviour as about the model itself.

work_description: Lead a team of 5; own the demand-forecasting platform covering 400k SKUs.
Cut forecast error (WMAPE) by 19% versus the previous model, directly reducing dead stock and stock-outs.
Designed geo-based experiments to measure marketing incrementality; reallocated 12% of budget to channels that actually drove profit.
Built a pricing elasticity model used by the commercial team for seasonal promotions.
Established code review and reproducible-training standards across the team.
Built credit-risk and churn models in production; one early-warning model reduced missed repayments materially.
Set up the model monitoring and fairness-review process with the risk function.
Delivered forecasting and segmentation projects for retail and telecom clients.
Wrote the internal guide to experiment design still used by new joiners.
Survey analysis and dashboards; moved into modelling after automating a forecasting prototype.

description: Reconciled SKU-store to category forecasts with a coherent bottom-up/top-down method; inventory turns and availability both improved.
Reconciled SKU-store forecasts to category level; inventory turns improved measurably.
Quantified channel contribution with adstock and saturation effects, guiding a 12% budget reallocation.
Quantified channel contribution and guided budget reallocation.
Designed holdout regions to measure true marketing lift where A/B tests were impossible.
Using geo holdouts we measured the true lift of channels that could not be A/B tested, then moved 12% of the budget to the channels that actually produced profit.
Survival model plus targeted offers; retention ROI reported monthly to the business.
Survival model plus targeted retention offers; retention ROI tracked and reported monthly.
Published an internal library for time-series backtesting adopted by two other teams.
Built a backtesting toolkit for time-series models now used by two other teams.

The legacy model ignored promotions and seasonality. Led a rebuild using gradient boosting with hierarchical reconciliation; forecast error dropped 19% and purchasing decisions changed measurably from the next season.
A survival model flagged deteriorating accounts weeks before formal delinquency; the risk team used it to restructure rather than default.
Estimated price sensitivity by category and promoted the promotions that were actually profitable rather than merely large.
Built a pricing elasticity model used by the commercial team for seasonal promotions.

items: Decision focus: every model is framed around a decision and an expected value, not an accuracy score.
Production mindset: reproducible training, monitoring and ownership after launch are non-negotiable.
Team building: I have grown a team from 2 to 5, with clear career paths and a real review culture.
Communication: I explain uncertainty honestly so stakeholders can choose a threshold consciously.

custom_sections.section_title: HOW I LEAD A DATA SCIENCE TEAM
items: Clear problem framing: we define the decision, the metric and the guardrails before touching a model.
Reproducibility: versioned data, code review and MLflow from day one so results can be trusted and revisited.
Growth: each person owns a domain and presents their work; I coach on both method and communication.
Honest uncertainty: confidence intervals and assumptions are shared, not hidden behind a single number.
Frame the decision: no model starts until we agree what action it will change and how we will judge success.
Respect uncertainty: confidence intervals and clear assumptions are part of every deliverable.
Own it in production: monitoring, drift alerts and a named owner, or the model does not ship.
Teach the team: I explain methods so the team can challenge my choices, not just execute them.
Co-organiser of a Cluj data meetup; mentor in a women-in-tech programme (2 cohorts).
Wrote internal guides on backtesting and experiment design used across the data org.
Deep Learning Specialisation (Coursera, 2020).
Modelling: gradient boosting, time-series, hierarchical forecasting, survival analysis, causal inference
Engineering: Python, SQL, PySpark, Databricks, Airflow, MLflow, dbt, Git
Methods: experiment design, A/B and geo testing, uplift modelling, backtesting
: Head of Data Science at eMAG and a university supervisor - on request

raw_cv.summary: Data engineer with 9 years building lakehouse platforms. Now Senior Data Engineer at Amazon Development Center, Iasi: own 200+ pipelines feeding analytics and ML, cut batch cost 35% with Delta optimisation and smarter partitioning. Strong in Spark, Kafka, Airflow, dbt and in making data people trust (tests, contracts, lineage).

work_description: Lead the ingestion layer (Kafka + Spark Structured Streaming) for 40 source systems, 2B events/day.
Cut pipeline cost 35% and runtime 50% via Delta Z-ordering, compaction and partition redesign.
Introduced dbt + data contracts and 3,000 freshness/schema tests; broken-dashboard incidents -80%.
Mentor 3 engineers; own the on-call runbook for the data platform.
Built an on-prem-to-cloud warehouse migration (Oracle to Redshift + dbt); 60 reports replatformed.
Automated reconciliation that caught EUR 2M of reporting drift.
Modeled production KPIs in SQL Server; plants finally agreed on one definition of OEE.

description: Moved 40 sources to Kafka + Spark Structured Streaming with exactly-once semantics; end-to-end freshness under 5 minutes.
Delta optimisation, compaction and partition strategy cut storage and compute 35%; documented as a reusable runbook.
Introduced dbt tests + contracts at the source boundary; broken-dashboard incidents down 80% year over year.
Delivered a Delta-based feature store that unblocked the ML team in 6 weeks.

work_description: Own AWS organisation guardrails (SCPs, permission boundaries, break-glass) across 300 accounts and 900 developers.

Chair the IaC security guild; 220 PRs/month reviewed, false-positive rate held under 8%.
Built cloud detection content and EDR tuning for an enterprise product; MTTD 30 to 9 minutes.
Delivered 40+ internal pentests and remediation guidance that developers actually adopted.
Firewalls, VPN and Linux fleets; on-call for backbone incidents; started automating with Ansible.

description: Replaced VPN with identity-aware access for 900 developers.

Reduced access-related incidents by 55% (-55%).
Migrated 3 tools into Splunk + Sentinel.
Rationalised 1,400 detection rules to 300 high-signal rules.
Measurably reduced alert fatigue.
Security workstream for 40 workloads moving to AWS.
Performed a threat model per workload.
All critical findings were fixed before go-live.
Built a 6-module internal course.
500 engineers completed the course.
Reduced secret-leak incidents in Git by 80% (-80%).

raw_cv.summary: Consultant radiologist (medic primar) with 24 years in diagnostic imaging, now at Institutul Clinic Fundeni, Bucharest. Subspecialties: abdominal MRI, oncology staging and CT angiography. Report 7,000-8,000 studies/year, coordinate residents and run the MRI protocol committee. Known for precise, decision-ready reports and for talking to the referring clinician before the patient leaves.

work_description: Interpret 7,000-8,000 CT/MRI studies/year; lead abdominal MRI and hepatobiliary imaging.
Chair the MRI protocol committee; standardised 40 protocols across two scanners.
Co-supervise 6 radiology residents; run a weekly case mammography-meeting-style review.
Emergency and trauma CT; 24h on-call rota; introduced structured trauma reporting.
Rotations across CT, MRI, ultrasound, mammography and interventional basics.

description: A gestionat un portofoliu de 12 firme micro si mici din productie, servicii si comert, de la contabilitate primara la balanta si decontari.

Terapie: CBT, terapie de expunere, EMDR, terapia Acceptarii si Angajamentului (ACT)

raw_cv.raw_text:
Radu Nistoroiu
Marine Biologist - coastal ecology & conservation - 8 years
Constanta | +40 748 330 118 | radu.nistoroiu.bio@gmail.com | linkedin.com/in/radu-nistoroiu
PROFILE
Marine biologist with 8 years studying Black Sea coastal ecosystems, from seagrass meadows to fish populations and water
quality. I run field surveys, analyse the data and translate findings into conservation advice. I have worked on EU-funded
monitoring projects and published in regional journals.
EXPERIENCE
Research Biologist 2018 - Present
Marine research institute - Constanta
(cid:127) Design and run coastal monitoring surveys (water, sediments, biodiversity).
(cid:127) Analyse datasets and contribute to EU reporting on marine environmental status.
(cid:127) Supervise 2-3 field assistants and coordinate sampling campaigns.
Field Biologist 2015 - 2018
NGO conservation project - Black Sea coast
(cid:127) Biodiversity monitoring and community outreach on coastal conservation.
SKILLS
Field: sampling design, SCUBA survey, species identification, water-quality methods
Analysis: R, GIS basics, statistics, scientific writing and reporting
SELECTED WORK
(cid:127) Seagrass mapping (2021): mapped meadow extent along a 40 km stretch and flagged loss hotspots.
(cid:127) Fish survey (2019): contributed to a multi-year dataset on coastal fish populations.
(cid:127) Outreach (2017): ran school workshops on the Black Sea ecosystem.
EDUCATION AND LANGUAGES
B.Sc. Biology (2007-2010), M.Sc. Marine Ecology (2010-2012). Several papers in regional journals. Romanian native, English
C1.
PUBLICATIONS AND REPORTS
(cid:127) Contributions to EU marine-environment status reporting.
(cid:127) Co-author of regional journal papers on Black Sea coastal ecology.
(cid:127) Technical reports on seagrass extent and water quality for funders.
FIELD AND LABORATORY SKILLS
(cid:127) Survey: sampling design, SCUBA transects and species identification.
(cid:127) Lab: water and sediment analysis, basic statistics, data archiving.
(cid:127) Reporting: clear scientific writing and stakeholder briefings.


PROJECTS
(cid:127) Seagrass meadow mapping along a 40 km coastal stretch.
(cid:127) Multi-year coastal fish-population dataset.
(cid:127) School outreach on Black Sea conservation.

raw_cv.summary: Engineering manager with 12 years in software, the last 6 leading teams of 6 to 14 engineers. I build the conditions where good engineers stay and ship calmly: clear goals, sane on-call, and a culture where problems surface early. At a marketplace in Bucharest I manage the payments platform group, two teams and about 18 engineers. I still read code weekly and I still believe software engineering management is engineering.

work_description: Lead 2 teams (18 engineers) owning the payments and payouts platform.

raw_cv.summary: Medic primar pediatru cu 18 ani de experienta in ingrijirea copilului, de la nou-nascut la adolescent, intr-un spital clinic din Iasi. Am coordonat sectia de pediatrie cu 40 de paturi si am dezvoltat un program de urmarire a prematurilor. Cred ca un consult bun inseamna sa intelegi copilul, nu doar boala, si sa explici parintelui pe intelesul lui.

work_description: Coordonez sectia de pediatrie (40 de paturi, 14 medici si asistente) si programul de urmarire a prematurilor.
Am redus reinternarile pentru astm si deshidratare printr-un program educativ pentru parinti.
Am implementat ghiduri de antibioticoterapie rationala, cu rezultate bune si fara complicatii.
Consultanter in garda de pediatrie si in unitatea de primiri urgente pentru cazurile complexe.
Pediatrie generala, neonatologie, urgente; am dezvaluit interesul pentru prematuri si adolescenti.
Stagii pe pediatrie, neonatologie si urgente; peste 2.000 de consultatii.

raw_cv.raw_text:
Dr. Roxana Balan
Medic Primar Pediatru - Pediatrie si nou-nascuti
Iasi | +40 746 330 118 | dr.roxana.balan@gmail.com | Colegiul Medicilor Iasi
PROFIL
Medic primar pediatru cu 18 ani de experienta in ingrijirea copilului, de la nou-nascut la adolescent, intr-un
spital clinic din Iasi. Am coordonat sectia de pediatrie cu 40 de paturi si am dezvoltat un program de urmarire
a prematurilor. Cred ca un consult bun inseamna sa intelegi copilul, nu doar boala, si sa explici parintelui pe
intelesul lui.
STUDII
Period Etapa Institutie
2006-2007 Atestat neonatologie UMF Iasi
2002-2006 Rezidentiat pediatrie UMF Iasi / Spitalul de Copii
1996-2002 Facultatea de Medicina UMF Grigore T. Popa Iasi
EXPERIENTA
Medic Primar Pediatru / Coordonator sectie 2012 - Prezent
Spitalul de Copii - Iasi
(cid:127) Coordonez sectia de pediatrie (40 de paturi, 14 medici si asistente) si programul de urmarire a
prematurilor.
(cid:127) Am redus reinternarile pentru astm si deshidratare printr-un program educativ pentru parinti.
(cid:127) Am implementat ghiduri de antibioticoterapie rationala, cu rezultate bune si fara complicatii.
(cid:127) Consultanter in garda de pediatrie si in unitatea de primiri urgente pentru cazurile complexe.
Medic Specialist Pediatru 2006 - 2012
Spitalul de Copii - Iasi
(cid:127) Pediatrie generala, neonatologie, urgente; am dezvaluit interesul pentru prematuri si adolescenti.
Medic Rezident Pediatrie 2002 - 2006
UMF Iasi
(cid:127) Stagii pe pediatrie, neonatologie si urgente; peste 2.000 de consultatii.
COMPETENTE
Clinice: pediatrie generala, neonatologie, astm si alergologie, boli infectioase, adolescentologie
Proceduri: consiliere parinti, educatie pentru ingrijirea prematurilor, interpretare investigatii
Organizare: coordonare sectie, ghiduri clinice, formarea rezidentilor


REALIZARI
(cid:127) Programul prematurilor: urmarire structurata pana la 3 ani, cu screening de dezvoltare.
(cid:127) Educatie parinti: sesiuni lunare despre febra, alimentatie si urgente; mai putine prezentari nejustificate la
garda.
(cid:127) Publicatii: 10 articole si prezentari la congrese de pediatrie.
(cid:127) Vaccinare: sustinerea programului de vaccinare si a educatiei antivaccinare in comunitate.
INFORMATII SUPLIMENTARE
Limbi: romana nativa, engleza B2, franceza A2. Afilieri: Societatea de Pediatrie. Consimtamant GDPR
pentru prelucrarea datelor in scop de recrutare.
ACTIVITATE SI REZULTATE
(cid:127) Programul prematurilor: urmarire structurata pana la 3 ani, cu screening de dezvoltare si consilierea
parintilor.
(cid:127) Astmul copilului: plan de actiune scris pentru fiecare copil cu astm; mai putine urgentari severe.
(cid:127) Antibioticoterapie rationala: ghiduri interne implementate, cu rezultate clinice bune si fara complicatii.
(cid:127) Educatia parintilor: sesiuni lunare despre febra, alimentatie si urgente pediatrice.
FORMARE SI DEZVOLTARE PROFESIONALA
(cid:127) Atestat in neonatologie; cursuri de pneumologie pediatric si alergologie.
(cid:127) Publicatii si prezentari la congrese nationale de pediatrie.
(cid:127) Formator intern pentru rezidentii din sectie.
INFORMATII SUPLIMENTARE
Disponibilitate: Cerinte conform Colegiului Medicilor; garda si UPU pediatrie
Referinte: Managerul spitalului si seful de sectie - la cerere
Limbi: romana nativa, engleza B2, franceza A2. Afilieri: Societatea Romana de Pediatrie. Consimtamant

work_description: Own commercial contracting: SaaS subscriptions, licensing, procurement and partner agreements across EU and UK.
Built a template and playbook library that cut average contract turnaround from 12 to 4 days.
Lead privacy work (GDPR) including DPIAs, data-processing agreements and a vendor risk framework.
Advise product and engineering on licensing, open-source and IP questions.
Commercial contracts, consumer protection and dispute management for a multi-country retailer.
Commercial litigation and corporate work; the training that made me a better in-house lawyer.

description: Introduced templates, negotiation playbooks and a self-serve portal; turnaround cut from 12 to 4 days.
DPIAs, DPAs and a vendor risk framework across 6 jurisdictions with no regulatory findings.
A licence review process that unblocked engineering while keeping IP safe.
Legal workstream for two acquisitions, including due diligence and integration contracts.

items: Contract velocity: turnaround cut from 12 to 4 days with templates, a playbook and a self-serve portal.
Privacy programme: reached and maintained GDPR compliance across 6 jurisdictions with no regulatory findings.
Risk reduction: renegotiated supplier contracts to add liability caps, audit rights and clear SLAs.
Training: ran internal sessions that reduced ad-hoc legal escalations from the business by roughly a third.
Business-partner mindset: I look for the deal structure that manages risk instead of only saying no.
Systems over heroics: templates, playbooks and a self-serve portal reduce turnaround and let me focus on the hard deals.
Training the business: the more the teams understand, the fewer escalations and the better the contracts.
Deals: negotiate and close a mix of customer, procurement and partner agreements across the EU and UK.
Legal reviews: advise product and engineering on licensing, IP and data questions, usually within a day.
Compliance: run DPIAs, review vendors and keep the privacy register and policies current.
Enablement: update templates and playbooks, and train the sales and product teams.
Commercial contracts: SaaS subscriptions, licensing, procurement, distribution, reseller and partner deals

raw_cv.summary: Medic primar radiolog cu 21 de ani de experiennn în imagisticn medicaln, la un centru de imagisticn din Cluj-Napoca. Interpret CT, RM si ecografie pentru peste 9.000 de studii pe an, cu sub-specializare pe imagistica neuro, musculo-scheletica si abdominala. Coordonez protocolul de calitate al centrului si formez rezidentii. Cred ca un diagnostic bun începe cu o întrebare clinica precisa si cu o comunicare clara a rezultatului.

work_description: Interpretez peste 9.000 de studii pe an (CT, RM, ecografie) cu sub-specializare neuro, MSK si abdominala.
Coordonez protocolul de calitate: dozimetrie, protectia radiological, timpi de raportare.
Formez rezidentii si coordonez sesiunile de caz; doua protocoale ale centrului sunt folosite si in alte centre.
Colaborez cu chirurgi, ortopedi si neurologi pentru corelarea clinico-imagistica.
Imagistica clinica completa, garda si urgente; primele sub-specializari pe neuro si MSK.
Formare completa in radiologie; peste 3.000 de studii interpretate cu supervizare.

items: Protocoale de RM: optimizarea secventelor pentru neuro si MSK; timpi de examinare redusi cu mentinerea calitatii.

Publicatii: 14 articole in reviste de specialitate si multiple prezentari la congrese.
Coord. de curs: lector la cursuri de imagistica si atelier de ecografie pentru rezidenti.
Neuroimagistica: protocoale RM pentru patologia demielinizanta, tumori ni patologia vasculara; colaborare cu neurologia.
Musculo-scheletic: RM si ecografie pentru genunchi, umar si coloana; corelare cu ortopedia si medicina sportiva.

Urgente: CT in garda pentru politrauma, AVC si patologia abdominala acuta.

Permit renewal for a large industrial site.

raw_cv.summary: Forensic accountant and expert witness with 19 years in the field, half in Big 4 forensic teams and half in independent practice. I investigate fraud, quantify losses, and prepare expert reports courts and arbitral tribunals accept. My work has supported both criminal cases and commercial disputes worth several million euros, and I have testified as an expert in court.

work_description: Lead fraud investigations and loss quantification; prepare expert reports for courts and arbitration.
Have testified as an expert witness in several cases.
Work with lawyers, regulators and company boards on asset tracing and recovery.
Managed fraud investigations, compliance reviews and litigation support across CEE.
Led teams of up to 8 on multi-jurisdiction cases.
Audit and forensic fundamentals; evidence gathering and documentation.

description: Traced a kickback scheme through supplier records; report supported a criminal case.
Quantified losses from diverted revenue in a EUR 8M arbitration.
Followed funds across three jurisdictions to support recovery.
Investigated internal allegations and recommended control fixes.
Flagged undisclosed related-party dealings before closing.

Natalia Fischer
Urban Planner - mobility & zoning - 16 years
Cluj-Napoca | +40 745 331 002 | natalia.fischer.plan@gmail.com | linkedin.com/in/natalia-fischer-plan
PROFILE
Urban planner with 16 years working on zoning, mobility and public-space strategies for cities and regions. I
have led general urban plans, mobility studies and participatory planning processes, and I am comfortable
both with regulation and with the messy reality of negotiating with communities, developers and officials. My
work has shaped how several mid-size Romanian cities grow and move.
EXPERIENCE
Lead Urban Planner 2015 - Present
Planning consultancy - Cluj-Napoca

Planning studio - Cluj

AREAS OF EXPERTISE
Planning: general urban plans, zoning regulation, mobility and parking, urban regeneration
Process: public consultation, stakeholder facilitation, feasibility and impact studies
Tools: GIS, AutoCAD, urban analysis, statistics, plan drafting
SELECTED PROJECTS
(cid:127) City mobility plan (2021): led a strategy that rebalanced street space toward transit, cycling and walking.
(cid:127) Urban regeneration (2019): a riverside public-space plan delivered through a participatory process.
(cid:127) Zoning update (2023): revised a zoning code to allow gentle density while protecting heritage.
(cid:127) Regional strategy (2018): a multi-city growth study that guided infrastructure investment.
APPROACH
(cid:127) Evidence and people: good plans combine data with what residents actually experience.


(cid:127) Long horizon: decisions are made for the next 20 years, not just the next election.
(cid:127) Implementation: a plan that cannot be delivered is a document, not a plan.

(cid:127) School-streets pilot (2021): safer routes to school delivered with parents and police.
(cid:127) Flood-resilience review (2019): integrated blue-green corridors into zoning.
METHODOLOGY
(cid:127) Evidence and people: combine data with lived experience through structured consultation.
(cid:127) Long horizon: plan for the next 20 years, not the next electoral cycle.

raw_cv.summary: Financial controller with 13 years in manufacturing and FMCG, owning controlling, budgeting and management reporting for plants of up to EUR 120M revenue. I make numbers that managers actually use: a monthly pack that explains variance, not a binder nobody reads. I have led cost-reduction programmes, standard-cost resets and ERP migrations, and I like being close to the shop floor, not only to the spreadsheet.

work_description: Own controlling and management reporting for a plant with EUR 120M revenue and 700 employees.
Lead the budgeting and forecasting cycle; monthly close delivered in 5 working days.
Ran a cost-reduction programme that delivered EUR 2.3M annual savings in two years through material, yield and overhead initiatives tracked to the P&L.
Led the controlling workstream of an SAP migration; rebuilt product costing and standard costs from scratch for a clean go-live with no material reporting errors.
Reduced the monthly close cycle from 9 to 5 working days with better cut-off and automation.
Redesigned the monthly management pack so decisions are made from it, not despite it.
Ran CAPEX governance through business cases and post-completion reviews that stopped 2 weak projects and prioritised better ones.
Product costing, variance analysis and CAPEX business cases across two factories.
Financial analysis and reporting projects; built the costing foundation of my career.

description: Built and deployed a recommender in production.
Used a hybrid collaborative + content model.
Produced a small but measurable lift in CTR.
The hard part was cold start.
Built and deployed a churn model.
Reached approximately 0.79 ROC-AUC.
Used by the retention team as a signal, not a verdict.
The business value came from the process, not the model alone.
Performed demand forecasting for a subset of SKUs.
Obtained mixed results: some SKUs forecast well and others did not.
Documented both what worked and what did not work.
Learned a lot from what did not work.
Developed a ticket-classification prototype.
Reduced manual sorting in a pilot.

work_description: Own a product line: strategy, roadmap, discovery and delivery with 2 teams.
Ran discovery and pricing changes that improved retention.
Partner closely with sales and support to prioritise.
Owned a team backlog; introduced clearer acceptance criteria.
Requirements and process work; moved toward product.

items: Talk to customers, then talk to them again.
Prioritise with evidence and say no with a reason.
Keep the team close to the problem, not just the tickets.
Define success before building, and measure after.
I am a strong product person and a decent analyst, but I am not the most technical PM and I do not pretend to be. I rely on engineers for the hard technical calls, and I back them.
Discovery interviews, jobs-to-be-done and opportunity mapping.
Funnel and cohort analysis in Amplitude; basic SQL for ad-hoc questions.
A/B testing for changes worth testing, not for everything.
Context over tickets: teams get the why, not just the what.
Trade-offs: I bring options, not demands.
Trust: I defend technical quality, not just dates.
Learning: I ask the naive question early rather than late.
Interviews and support shadowing to see real friction.
Willing to kill features that do not earn their place.
Close the loop with customers when their feedback ships.
Activation (2022): onboarding rework that measurably lifted activation.
Pricing (2021): a packaging change that grew revenue without a churn spike.
Focus (2023): killed two features early, saving a quarter of engineering time.
I measure myself by outcomes for customers and the business, not by how many features shipped.
Sometimes the best product decision is the one we do not build.

items: Operable: designs a team can run matter more than elegant diagrams.

raw_cv.summary: Cloud solutions architect with 12 years in IT and six focused on AWS. I design landing zones, migrations and cost-aware architectures for enterprise and regulated clients. I enjoy the design conversation and the politics of it as much as the technology, and I am comfortable saying no to an architecture that will not survive production.

work_description: Designed multi-account AWS landing zones with guardrails and SSO.
Led migrations of legacy workloads with minimal downtime.
Established cost governance that cut cloud spend meaningfully.
Advised client teams on well-architected reviews and remediation.
Automation, IaC and early cloud adoption across several teams.
Designed hybrid connectivity between on-prem and cloud.
Windows/Linux administration and virtualisation.

projects.project_name: Landing zone and migration for regulated client
description: Context: a regulated client needed to move critical workloads to AWS safely.
What I did: designed the landing zone, migration path and guardrails with the client team.
Outcome: migration completed with tested rollback and no unplanned downtime.
Key lesson: the design only works if the client's own team can run it after handover.
a regulated client needed to move critical workloads to AWS safely.
designed the landing zone, migration path and guardrails with the client team.
migration completed with tested rollback and no unplanned downtime.

items: Requirements first: compliance, latency, budget and team skills before services.
Boring where possible: managed services over bespoke unless there is a reason.
Security by default: guardrails and least privilege, not afterthoughts.
Cost awareness: an architecture nobody can afford is not an architecture.
Handover: designs the client's own team can run after I leave.
Landing zone: multi-account AWS setup adopted as the enterprise standard.
Migration: critical workloads moved with tested rollback and minimal downtime.
Cost: governance that brought cloud spend under control without hurting delivery.
I am an architect and advisor, not a hands-on platform engineer day to day. I can build with Terraform, but I rely on strong engineers for deep implementation and I say so plainly.
AWS, Terraform, CloudFormation and Python for automation.
Security, finance and delivery stakeholders in every design.
Well-Architected reviews and pragmatic remediation plans.
Architecture that the client's team can actually run.

A good architecture is measured in the years after handover, not in the elegance of the diagram. I optimise for the team that inherits the system, and I am comfortable being the person who says the less exciting option is the right one.

I keep a lab where I try designs before proposing them, and I follow cost and security developments in cloud closely. Longer term I want to keep working at the intersection of architecture, cost and governance, where good decisions save companies real money.
Wrote reference architectures reused across client engagements.
Mentored junior engineers toward cloud certifications.
Ran internal sessions on cost and security governance.
Reviewed delivery designs for the well-architected pillars.

raw_cv.summary: IT project manager with 14 years delivering infrastructure, migration and datacentre projects for banks and industry. I run the plan, the risk and the difficult conversations, and I keep sponsors informed before they have to ask. I am a delivery person, not a hands‑on engineer any more, and I am clear about that boundary.

work_description: Led datacentre migrations and network refresh programmes.
Managed budgets, vendors and multi-team delivery schedules.
Ran steering committees and turned around two at-risk projects.
Delivered infrastructure and application rollout projects.
Coordinated subcontractors and reported to clients.
Internal IT projects and vendor management.

description: a datacentre migration with several vendors and a hard regulatory deadline.
rebuilt the plan, surfaced risk early and coordinated suppliers closely.
delivered on time with no unplanned downtime and a clean handover.
honest early communication costs far less than a late surprise.

items: Plan honestly: a realistic schedule beats an optimistic one that slips.
Surface risk early: bad news does not improve with age.
Protect the team: shield them from churn and politics where I can.
Keep sponsors informed: no surprises in steering committees.
Close properly: handover, documentation and lessons learned.
Datacentre migration: completed on time with no unplanned downtime.
Turnaround: two at-risk projects brought back under control.
Vendors: managed multi-supplier delivery without slippage.

I am a delivery manager, not the engineer who racks the servers. I understand infrastructure well enough to challenge estimates and ask the right questions, but the technical execution belongs to the engineers.
MS Project, Jira and Confluence for planning and reporting.
Budget tracking, vendor management and procurement.
Risk registers and clear escalation paths.
Both waterfall and agile delivery, chosen to fit the work.

I read about delivery and leadership as much as about technology, because most project problems are human. I am comfortable running large programmes and I would like to keep leading migrations where the stakes and the learning are both high.
Coached new project managers on planning and risk.
Ran lessons-learned reviews that changed how we plan.
Worked with procurement on vendor selection and contracts.
Kept stakeholders aligned across business and IT.

work_description: Own Kubernetes platform used by 40+ services and several teams.
Introduced SLOs and error budgets; cut noisy alerts substantially.
Built self-service deployment tooling to reduce toil for developers.
Led incident reviews and drove lasting fixes rather than patches.
CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code and container adoption.
Migrated services from VMs to containers with zero downtime cutover.
Linux servers, monitoring and on-call for customer platforms.

description: a growing platform was fragile and the team spent nights on repeat incidents.
defined SLOs, cut alert noise and automated the top sources of toil.
fewer pages, faster releases and developers who no longer waited on us.
reliability improves when developers own the services and the platform removes friction.

items: Measure: SLOs first, opinions second; the data decides where to invest.
Reduce toil: automate the repetitive before hiring around it.
Learn from incidents: blame-free reviews that change systems, not people.
Incident reduction: fewer repeat alerts after systemic fixes.
Developer velocity: self-service deploys cut waiting on the platform team.
Migration: a large workload moved off legacy hosts with no customer impact.
I am stronger on Linux, Kubernetes and reliability than on application code. I can read and fix code, but I hire for and defer to backend engineers on domain-heavy services.
Kubernetes, Helm and Argo for delivery at scale.
Terraform for infrastructure that survives review.
Prometheus and Grafana for observability that people use.
Python and bash for the glue nobody else wants to write.
Outside work I read incident post-mortems from other companies, because the best lessons are usually in someone else's outage.
I am deepening my knowledge of distributed systems and cost-aware reliability, and I would like to keep growing toward a staff-level platform role.
Wrote internal guides on running safe migrations and post-mortems.
Ran onboarding for new platform engineers.
Reviewed architecture proposals from product teams.
Kept an eye on cloud cost as part of reliability work.

HOW I APPROACH RELIABILITY
(cid:127) Measure: SLOs first, opinions second; the data decides where to invest.
(cid:127) Reduce toil: automate the repetitive before hiring around it.
(cid:127) Learn from incidents: blame-free reviews that change systems, not people.

(cid:127) Developer velocity: self-service deploys cut waiting on the platform team.
(cid:127) Migration: a large workload moved off legacy hosts with no customer impact.
A NOTE ON WEAKNESSES
I am stronger on Linux, Kubernetes and reliability than on application code. I can read and fix code, but I hire
for and defer to backend engineers on domain-heavy services.
TOOLING AND STACK
(cid:127) Kubernetes, Helm and Argo for delivery at scale.
(cid:127) Terraform for infrastructure that survives review.
(cid:127) Prometheus and Grafana for observability that people use.
(cid:127) Python and bash for the glue nobody else wants to write.
A CLOSING NOTE
Reliability is a habit more than a tool. I would rather leave a team with fewer alerts, clearer runbooks and the
confidence to change things safely than with an impressive architecture diagram and the wrong kind of
excitement at 3am.
SELECTED PROJECT DEEP-DIVE
(cid:127) Context: a growing platform was fragile and the team spent nights on repeat incidents.
(cid:127) What I did: defined SLOs, cut alert noise and automated the top sources of toil.
(cid:127) Outcome: fewer pages, faster releases and developers who no longer waited on us.
(cid:127) Key lesson: reliability improves when developers own the services and the platform removes friction.
INTERESTS AND GROWTH
Outside work I read incident post-mortems from other companies, because the best lessons are usually in
someone else's outage. I am deepening my knowledge of distributed systems and cost-aware reliability, and I
would like to keep growing toward a staff-level platform role.
BEYOND THE DAY JOB
(cid:127) Wrote internal guides on running safe migrations and post-mortems.
(cid:127) Ran onboarding for new platform engineers.
(cid:127) Reviewed architecture proposals from product teams.
(cid:127) Kept an eye on cloud cost as part of reliability work.
HOW TO GET THE MOST OUT OF ME


Give me a system that hurts and the freedom to fix the root cause, and I will quietly make it boring. Give me a
deadline and a checklist instead, and you will get the checklist. I do my best work where reliability is treated as
an engineering problem rather than a firefighting shift, and where the team owns the outcome together.
A CLOSING NOTE
I have carried a pager long enough to know that the goal is not heroic recovery but a quiet night. I build
platforms and habits so that fewer things break, and so the things that do break are caught before customers
ever notice.

(cid:127) What I did: defined SLOs, cut alert noise and automated the top sources of toil.
(cid:127) Outcome: fewer pages, faster releases and developers who no longer waited on us.
(cid:127) Key lesson: reliability improves when developers own the services and the platform removes friction.
INTERESTS AND GROWTH
Outside work I read incident post-mortems from other companies, because the best lessons are usually in
someone else's outage. I am deepening my knowledge of distributed systems and cost-aware reliability, and I
would like to keep growing toward a staff-level platform role.
BEYOND THE DAY JOB
(cid:127) Wrote internal guides on running safe migrations and post-mortems.
(cid:127) Ran onboarding for new platform engineers.
(cid:127) Reviewed architecture proposals from product teams.
(cid:127) Kept an eye on cloud cost as part of reliability work.
HOW TO GET THE MOST OUT OF ME


Give me a system that hurts and the freedom to fix the root cause, and I will quietly make it boring. Give me a
deadline and a checklist instead, and you will get the checklist. I do my best work where reliability is treated as
an engineering problem rather than a firefighting shift, and where the team owns the outcome together.
A CLOSING NOTE
I have carried a pager long enough to know that the goal is not heroic recovery but a quiet night. I build
platforms and habits so that fewer things break, and so the things that do break are caught before customers
ever notice.

raw_cv.summary: Inginer de sisteme pentru calcul intensiv si centre de date, cu 15 ani in medii de cercetare si industry. Am crescut de la administrator de retea la proiectant de cluster HPC si am vazut cu ochi cum se schimba hardware-ul din 2010 incoa. Sunt pragmatic: prefer un plan de capacitate pe hartie decat un incident de productie la ora 2 dimineana.

work_description: Administrare si extindere a clusterului HPC cu Slurm si InfiniBand.
Benchmarking, planificare de capacitate si optimizare a joburilor.
Automatizare cu Ansible si Python; interventii de urgenta in cluster.
Documentatie si training pentru cercetatori in utilizarea clusterului.
Proiectare si operare a infrastructurii de virtualizare (VMware, KVM).
Depozitare pe obiect, retele de stocare si backup-uri la scara.
Monitorizare cu Zabbix si Grafana.
Administrare de retea, rutare si troubleshooting in noduri critice.

description: moved a 2,000-node HPC cluster to a new generation of hardware with no loss of queued work.
introduced a policy that cut storage cost by a third with no measurable slowdown for most users.
wrote the Ansible roles that now onboard a new node in under an hour.
re-planned rack density during a hall refurbishment, avoiding a costly retrofit.

items: Migrare cluster HPC de la retea 10G la 100G InfiniBand, cu zero downtime pentru joburile lungi.
Reducere cu 40% a timpului mediu de asteptare prin planificare mai buna a partitiilor.
Introducerea containerelor HPC in fluxul de lucru al cercetatorilor, fara schimbari majore de cod.
Procedura de disaster recovery testata si documentata pentru clusterul principal.
Cluster migration (2021): moved a 2,000-node HPC cluster to a new generation of hardware with no loss of queued work.
Storage tiering (2019): introduced a policy that cut storage cost by a third with no measurable slowdown for most users.
Automation suite (2018): wrote the Ansible roles that now onboard a new node in under an hour.
Power and cooling (2022): re-planned rack density during a hall refurbishment, avoiding a costly retrofit.
A storage incident in 2018 that froze a PhD student's four-month simulation; the post-mortem changed how I treat capacity warnings.
A failed procurement where the specification was mine and the supplier was right; I rewrote the tender template afterwards.
A period of two years with very little documentation around me, which is why I write so much now.
Many cluster users are domain scientists, not engineers, so the tooling has to be forgiving.
I keep job templates for common workloads so they rarely need to be modified by hand.
I train new users in the first session they need the cluster, never later.
I protect long-running jobs: a restart should never be anyone's default experience.
Slurm, Lustre, GPFS, InfiniBand and Ethernet fabrics.
Ansible, Python, Salt (legacy), Bash, Git and CI for infrastructure changes.
Grafana, Prometheus, Zabbix for monitoring and alerting.
Proxmox, VMware, Ceph, Nutanix for the surrounding infrastructure.
I follow the Slurm and RDMA development closely and test the notable releases in the lab.
I write internal notes on cluster operations that the new hires read first.
I am learning more about liquid cooling and high-density racks, which is where the field is going.
I restore old workstations as a side hobby, which is a good way to keep an old kernel build in shape.

I am an operations-minded systems engineer. I write good scripts, but I am not a full-time software developer, and the deep application-level debugging belongs to the people who build the applications. I have also led less work on cost commercial side than I would like, because I find that less interesting than the machines.
Administration and operation of the main HPC cluster, including the scheduler and the parallel filesystem.
Capacity forecasting, hardware refresh planning and budget preparation for the compute budget.
On-call rotation for the cluster, together with a small team of two peers.
Training for new users and the operation of a documentation portal for the institute.
Un sistem de monitorizare care priveste de la job si nu de la masina, cu alertare pe nivel de utilizator.
O politica de prioritizare intre cercetatori, negociata cu conducerea si revizuita anual.
Un pipeline de instalare a software pentru cercetatori, care a eliminat instalarea manuala de doua zile.

custom_sections.section_title: DE CE AM RAMAS IN CERCETARE
items: Cercetatorii au probleme pe care nu le gasesti intr-un catalog de produse, si asta este o provocare care ma tine treaz.
Institutul are o latura de aplicare a cercetarii in industria locala, iar eu coordonez partea de calcul.
Masura mea de reusita este un cluster plin si nimeni care sa stea la coada in zori.

In decenii de centre de date am vazut echipe cu cel mai bun hardware sa esueze din lipsa de proceduri, si echipe cu hardware modest sa mearga bine prin disciplina de operare. (cid:127) Measure honestly: queue time, failure rate and energy, not just uptime.
SELECTED WORK
(cid:127) Cluster migration (2021): moved a 2,000-node HPC cluster to a new generation
of hardware with no loss of queued work.
(cid:127) Storage tiering (2019): introduced a policy that cut storage cost by a third
with no measurable slowdown for most users.
(cid:127) Automation suite (2018): wrote the Ansible roles that now onboard a new node
in under an hour.
(cid:127) Power and cooling (2022): re-planned rack density during a hall refurbishment,
avoiding a costly retrofit.
DIFFICULT MOMENTS


(cid:127) A storage incident in 2018 that froze a PhD student's four-month simulation;
the post-mortem changed how I treat capacity warnings.
(cid:127) A failed procurement where the specification was mine and the supplier was
right; I rewrote the tender template afterwards.
(cid:127) A period of two years with very little documentation around me, which is why I
write so much now.
WORKING WITH RESEARCHERS
(cid:127) Many cluster users are domain scientists, not engineers, so the tooling has to
be forgiving.
(cid:127) I keep job templates for common workloads so they rarely need to be modified by
hand.
(cid:127) I train new users in the first session they need the cluster, never later.
(cid:127) I protect long-running jobs: a restart should never be anyone's default
experience.
TOOLS AND ENVIRONMENTS
(cid:127) Slurm, Lustre, GPFS, InfiniBand and Ethernet fabrics.
(cid:127) Ansible, Python, Salt (legacy), Bash, Git and CI for infrastructure changes.
(cid:127) Grafana, Prometheus, Zabbix for monitoring and alerting.
(cid:127) Proxmox, VMware, Ceph, Nutanix for the surrounding infrastructure.
INTERESTS AND LEARNING
(cid:127) I follow the Slurm and RDMA development closely and test the notable releases
in the lab.
(cid:127) I write internal notes on cluster operations that the new hires read first.
(cid:127) I am learning more about liquid cooling and high-density racks, which is where
the field is going.
(cid:127) I restore old workstations as a side hobby, which is a good way to keep an old
kernel build in shape.
A NOTE ON WEAKNESSES
I am an operations-minded systems engineer. I write good scripts, but I am not a
full-time software developer, and the deep application-level debugging belongs to
the people who build the applications. I have also led less work on cost
commercial side than I would like, because I find that less interesting than the
machines.
RESPONSABILITATI CURENTE


(cid:127) Administration and operation of the main HPC cluster, including the scheduler
and the parallel filesystem.
(cid:127) Capacity forecasting, hardware refresh planning and budget preparation for the
compute budget.
(cid:127) On-call rotation for the cluster, together with a small team of two peers.
(cid:127) Training for new users and the operation of a documentation portal for the
institute.
CE AM CONSTRUIT CU ECHIPA
(cid:127) Un sistem de monitorizare care priveste de la job si nu de la masina, cu
alertare pe nivel de utilizator.
(cid:127) O politica de prioritizare intre cercetatori, negociata cu conducerea si
revizuita anual.
(cid:127) Un pipeline de instalare a software pentru cercetatori, care a eliminat
instalarea manuala de doua zile.
DE CE AM RAMAS IN CERCETARE
(cid:127) Cercetatorii au probleme pe care nu le gasesti intr-un catalog de produse, si
asta este o provocare care ma tine treaz.
(cid:127) Institutul are o latura de aplicare a cercetarii in industria locala, iar eu
coordonez partea de calcul.
(cid:127) Masura mea de reusita este un cluster plin si nimeni care sa stea la coada in
zori.
GANDURI DE FINAL
In decenii de centre de date am vazut echipe cu cel mai bun hardware sa esueze
din lipsa de proceduri, si echipe cu hardware modest sa mearga bine prin
disciplina de operare. Nu cred in tehnologie fara practici, iar practicile se pot
invata, documenta si transmite, exact ce am incercat sa fac in fiecare rol pe
care l-am avut.

raw_cv.raw_text:
George Berindei
Hardware Design Engineer - PCB / EMC - 9 years
Bucharest | +40 721 663 004 | george.berindei.hw@gmail.com | linkedin.com/in/george-berindei-hw
PROFILE
Hardware design engineer with 9 years in PCB design, from schematics and stack-up to EMC compliance
and production support. I started in avionics, where the cost of a mistake is measured in a different currency,
and I still carry that habit of checking things twice. I am strong on Altium and on getting a design through
manufacturing the first time.
EXPERIENCE
Senior Hardware Engineer 2019 - Present
Medical devices company - Bucharest
(cid:127) Design of 4-layer and 6-layer PCBs for diagnostic devices.
(cid:127) EMC pre-compliance testing and design changes to meet IEC 60601 limits.
(cid:127) Component selection, BOM management and supplier coordination.
(cid:127) Hardware-software bring-up with firmware engineers.
Hardware Engineer 2016 - 2019
Avionics supplier - Bucharest
(cid:127) Design for rugged avionics boards, working to DO-160 environmental requirements.
(cid:127) Schematic capture, PCB stack-up selection and signal integrity reviews.
PCB Designer 2014 - 2016
Electronics manufacturer - Bucharest
(cid:127) Layout and documentation for production of existing designs.
SKILLS
Design: Altium Designer, KiCad, OrCAD Capture, schematic and layout
Analysis: EMC testing, signal integrity basics, thermal analysis, DFM/DFA
Process: PCB fabrication, assembly, bring-up, ECO management
CERTIFICATIONS
(cid:127) IPC-A-610 Certified Specialist (2018).
(cid:127) EMC fundamentals, TDK training (2021).
EDUCATION & LANGUAGES
B.Sc. Electrical Engineering, Politehnica Bucharest. Romanian native, English C1, French B2.


PROIECTE SELECTATE
(cid:127) Placa de diagnostic (2022): design pe 6 straturi, cu alimentare izolata si comunicatie izolata pentru
siguranta pacientului.
(cid:127) Redesign EMC (2021): refacerea planului de masa si filtrare, dupa esec la pre-compliance.
(cid:127) Avionica (2018): placi cu cerinte de vibratii si temperaturi extreme, verificate in laborator.
CUM LUCREZ
(cid:127) Fac revizie de schema inainte de layout, nu dupa.
(cid:127) Tin cont de DFM de la prima zi, pentru ca de multe ori PCB-ul se reface din cauza asta.
(cid:127) Testez cu analizor de retea si cu prototip real, nu doar in simulator.
(cid:127) Caut implicarea echipei de productie devreme: ei vad problemele pe care le vad rareori.
CE A FOST MAI GREU
(cid:127) In avionica am invatat sa lucrez sub incertitudine: unele conditii de test nu pot fi reproduse decat la sol, si
asta schimba felul in care proiectezi.
(cid:127) In medical am intalnit lupta intre cost si conformitate, unde alegerea nu este intotdeauna cea evidenta.
(cid:127) Am invatat sa comunic riscul tehnic in limbaj pe care directorii de produs il inteleg.
CERTIFICARI
(cid:127) IPC-A-610 Certified Specialist (2018).
(cid:127) Curs EMC fundamentals, TDK (2021).
(cid:127) Sediu de proiectare si design rules, Siemens (2019).
UN CUVANT DE FINAL
Ingineria hardware are o frumusate care nu apare in prezentari: poti sa atingi ce ai proiectat si sa stii ca
functioneaza. Am ramas in domeniu pentru asta, desi recompensele materiale nu sunt spectaculoase.
CE IMI PLACE CEL MAI MULT
(cid:127) Momentul in care prototipul se ridica prima data si functioneaza, cu toate semnalele la locul lor.
(cid:127) Discutia cu un designer de circuit integrat despre un pin, unde nimeni nu are ego si toti stiu mai mult decat
o singura persoana.
(cid:127) Faptul ca un design bun se vede si in costul de fabricatie, nu doar in functionare.
CE AS VREA SA SCHIMB
(cid:127) Proiectele se comenteaza prea tarziu, uneori dupa ce placa a fost deja comandata.


(cid:127) Documentatia PCB se face de multe ori pe loc, iar eu as prefera sa fie scrisa o data, bine, si refolosita.
(cid:127) As vrea sa lucrez intr-o echipa in care procesul de proiectare include si partea de testare, nu doar desenul.
